1.title: Workspaces, Apps and Distribution
1.text: Welcome to Module fourteen: Workspaces, Apps and Distribution. It covers the exam area Manage and secure Power B I. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Create and configure a workspace. Configure and update an app. Publish, import, or update items in a workspace. Create dashboards. Choose a distribution method. Configure subscriptions and data alerts. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Manage and secure Power B I (fifteen-twenty percent). Exam format: a one hundred-minute proctored exam; a score of seven hundred on a scale to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official P L three hundred study guide, skills measured as of April twenty, twenty twenty-six.

1.title: Workspaces and apps
1.text: Workspaces and apps. A workspace is where a team builds and manages content. An app is how finished content reaches consumers.

1.title: Workspaces and apps, continued
1.text: Workspaces and apps. The figure shows this: Content flows from a workspace to colleagues by role, to consumers through an app, and to single items by link, subscription, embed or export.

1.title: Workspaces and apps, continued
1.text: Workspaces and apps. Create. In the service choose Workspaces, then New workspace; name it and pick a license mode. License mode. Pro or P P U, or a Premium or Fabric capacity; on Premium or F sixty-four and above, Viewers can use a free license. Roles. Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer, given to users or groups (Module fifteen). Limits. Up to one thousand items in a workspace; a Pro user can be in up to one thousand workspaces. My workspace. Personal space; Direct Lake is not supported there.

1.title: Workspaces and apps, continued
1.text: Workspaces and apps. How many. One app per workspace. Audiences. Up to twenty-five audiences; each sees only the content you choose. Audience options. Allow sharing, allow building content, allow access to hidden content. Who publishes. Admin and Member; a Contributor can update it only if an Admin allows. Licenses. Creating or updating needs Pro or P P U; consumers need Pro or P P U unless the workspace is on Premium or F sixty-four and above, where free users can view. To update an app, change the workspace content, then update the app. Consumers see the new version only after that. Exam tip: One workspace has one app, and one app can have many audiences. Two groups that need different reports from one workspace get one app with two audiences.

1.title: Publish, import, update and dashboards
1.text: Publish, import, update and dashboards. Publish from Desktop. On the Home tab choose Publish, then pick the workspace. Upload a.pbix. In the workspace choose Upload and pick the file. Get data in the service. Create a semantic model and report from files or databases online. Update. Publishing again with the same name replaces the report and its semantic model. Contributor or higher can add and change items.

1.title: Publish, import, update and dashboards, continued
1.text: Publish, import, update and dashboards. A dashboard is created in the service only, never in Desktop. It is one page of tiles pinned from reports, Excel, Q and A, images, text or video. Pin a whole report page to get a live page tile. Creating one needs edit permission, and Pro or P P U outside My workspace.

1.title: Publish, import, update and dashboards, continued
1.text: Publish, import, update and dashboards. Built in. Report: Desktop or service. Dashboard: Service only. Pages. Report: One or more. Dashboard: One page of tiles. Sources. Report: A semantic model. Dashboard: Tiles from many reports and models. Slicers and filters. Report: Yes. Dashboard: No. Data alerts. Report: No. Dashboard: Yes, on tiles. Exam tip: Dashboards exist only in the service, hold tiles from many reports, and have no slicers. If a question needs one page that mixes several models, think dashboard.

1.title: Choose a distribution method
1.text: Choose a distribution method. People build and edit together. Method: Workspace access. Recipients need: A workspace role. Many consumers, curated content, groups. Method: App with audiences. Recipients need: Pro or P P U, or a Premium or F sixty-four workspace. One item for a person or group. Method: Share link. Recipients need: Read by default; Pro or P P U unless the content is in Premium. Show a report inside another site or app. Method: Embed. Recipients need: Access to the report; publishing to the web is public.

1.title: Choose a distribution method, continued
1.text: Choose a distribution method. A regular email of a page. Method: Subscription. Recipients need: Pro or P P U, or content in Premium. A file copy of the data. Method: Export. Recipients need: The export setting; Build for underlying data. Exam tip: Workspace role for collaborators, app for broad consumers, share link for one item. If a scenario says "many readers, curated, different groups", the answer is the app.

1.title: Subscriptions, data alerts and endorsement
1.text: Subscriptions, data alerts and endorsement. On. Email subscription: A report or dashboard. Data alert: A dashboard tile from a card, gauge or K P I (numeric). Limit. Email subscription: Up to twenty-four per item. Data alert: Up to two hundred fifty alerts. Timing. Email subscription: Hourly, Daily, Weekly, Monthly or After data refresh. Data alert: Checked about hourly or daily. License. Email subscription: Pro or P P U, or content in Premium. Data alert: Pro outside My workspace.

1.title: Subscriptions, data alerts and endorsement, continued
1.text: Subscriptions, data alerts and endorsement. Notes. Email subscription: A full-report P D F or Power Point attachment needs Premium or P P U; subscribing others needs Contributor or higher. Data alert: Service only; only you see your alerts; works with Power Automate.

1.title: Subscriptions, data alerts and endorsement, continued
1.text: Subscriptions, data alerts and endorsement. To set an alert, open the tile's ellipsis, choose Manage alerts, then Add alert rule. Set the title, threshold, frequency and email. Endorsement helps people find trusted content. It has two levels, and it does not change who has access. Promoted. The content owner, or a member with write permission. The higher level. Only authorized reviewers that the Power B I admin chooses. It applies to semantic models, reports, apps and dataflows. Exam tip: Promoted can be set by the owner; the higher endorsement level only by authorized reviewers. A subscription sends a snapshot on a schedule; a data alert fires when a tile value crosses a threshold.

2.title: Gateways and scheduled refresh
2.text: Gateways and scheduled refresh. A gateway is Windows software that lets the service reach a source it cannot reach directly. It uses outbound connections only. It is needed for on-premises or private-network sources, for refresh, Direct Query and live connection. Cloud sources need none. Standard. Shared and centrally managed; supports Direct Query and live connection; can form clusters. Personal. One user; Import refresh only; cannot be shared. V net data gateway. Microsoft-managed, nothing to install; for sources in a virtual network. Direct Lake cannot use a gateway.

2.title: Gateways and scheduled refresh, continued
2.text: Gateways and scheduled refresh. Limit per day. Pro up to eight; P P U, Premium and Fabric up to forty-eight. Time zone. Times follow the time zone set for the model. Credentials. Set in the semantic model settings; only the owner changes them (others take over). Gateway. Map the model to one gateway connection; one gateway per model. Failures. Email to the owner; the schedule is disabled after four consecutive failures. Other. Daily quota resets at twelve:one A M; Refresh now is not counted. Exam tip: Pro: up to eight scheduled refreshes a day; Premium, P P U and Fabric: up to forty-eight. Four consecutive failures disable the schedule.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. A workspace holds six reports. The sales team must see two of them and the finance team must see four. What should an Admin do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Publish one app with two audiences and assign the reports. A workspace has one app, and audiences control which content each group sees.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. An Import semantic model sits in a Pro workspace and must refresh every thirty minutes all day. Which change meets the need? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Move the workspace to a P P U, Premium or Fabric capacity. Pro allows up to eight scheduled refreshes a day, while P P U, Premium and Fabric allow up to forty-eight.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A report uses Direct Query against a sequel Server database in the company's data center. Users open it in the service. What is required? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A standard mode gateway with a data source connection. An on-premises Direct Query source needs a standard gateway, since a personal gateway supports Import refresh only.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A manager wants an email whenever the daily revenue number on a dashboard falls below a target. What should the manager set up? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: A data alert on a tile pinned from a card visual. Data alerts work on numeric tiles from cards, gauges and K P Is and email when a threshold is crossed; a subscription sends a snapshot regardless of the value.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. The owner of a semantic model wants colleagues to see it as recommended content in search. Which action can the owner take? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Apply the Promoted endorsement to the model. An owner can promote content, while the higher level is set only by authorized reviewers and a sensitivity label does not endorse.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A team in a Pro-only workspace wants a weekly email subscription that attaches the full report as a P D F. What is required? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The report moved to a workspace on Premium or P P U. A full-report attachment needs Premium or P P U, which a Pro-only workspace does not provide.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many apps can one workspace have? Answer: One, with up to twenty-five audiences. Question two. Where can you create a dashboard? Answer: In the Power B I service only. Question three. How many scheduled refreshes a day does Pro allow? Answer: Up to eight (P P U, Premium and Fabric: up to forty-eight).

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. After how many consecutive failures is a scheduled refresh disabled? Answer: Four. Question five. Which gateway mode supports Import refresh only? Answer: Personal mode. Question six. What happens when you publish a.pbix with the same name to the same workspace? Answer: The existing report and semantic model are replaced.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Workspace: license mode; roles Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer; up to one thousand items. App: one per workspace; up to twenty-five audiences; Admin and Member publish. Publish: Desktop publish, upload a.pbix, Get data in the service; same name replaces. Dashboard: service only; one page of tiles; no slicers. Distribution: role for collaborators; app for consumers; share link for one item; embed; subscription; export. Subscription and alert: up to twenty-four subscriptions per item. Endorsement: Promoted by the owner; the higher level only by authorized reviewers. Gateway: needed for on-premises and private-network sources; standard, personal (Import only), V net; none for cloud. Scheduled refresh: Pro eight a day, others forty-eight; owner sets credentials; disabled after four failures.
